name: Islamic cosmic geography (al-akhira)
dom: Eschatology; the structure of the otherworld (al-akhira) comprising Paradise, Hell, the intermediate realm and their thresholds
note: Hub/organizing entity for the Qur'anic and classical-Islamic otherworldly topography. Not a single named place in scripture but the standard scholarly framing (Lange) of the akhira as a layered cosmos; introduced here as a structural hub.

name: Jannah (the Garden, Paradise)
dom: The abode of the blessed; the Garden of reward, conceived as multi-tiered with rivers, gardens and gates
note: Qur'anic al-janna, frequently in the plural jannat. Well attested across the Qur'an (e.g. Q 2:25, 13:35, 47:15) and classical eschatology (Lange).

name: Jannat al-Firdaus (the highest Paradise)
dom: The highest and most excellent level of Paradise, beneath the Throne, source of its rivers
note: Qur'anic al-firdaws (Q 18:107, 23:11). In hadith the loftiest part of Jannah, beneath the Arsh; a level within Jannah.

name: Jannat ʿAdn (the Garden of Eden / perpetual abode)
dom: The Gardens of perpetuity, an eschatological abode of the righteous
note: Qur'anic jannat ʿadn (Q 9:72, 13:23). Distinct from the primordial garden of Adam in scholarly reading; a named level of Jannah.

name: Dar al-Salam (the Abode of Peace)
dom: A Qur'anic name for Paradise as the abode of peace and well-being
note: Qur'anic dar al-salam (Q 6:127, 10:25); classical exegesis treats it as an appellation/level of Jannah.

name: Dar al-Qarar (the Abode of Permanence)
dom: The enduring final abode contrasted with the transient world
note: Qur'anic dar al-qarar (Q 40:39), the abiding home of the hereafter; in classical eschatology read as a name of Paradise (Lange).

name: The Eight Gates of Paradise (abwab al-janna)
dom: The set of eight gates of Jannah through which classes of the righteous enter
note: Hadith tradition (e.g. al-Bukhari) enumerates eight gates of Paradise (the gate of prayer, of fasting/al-Rayyan, of charity, etc.), against seven of Hell. Modeled here as a collective set.

name: Jahannam (Gehenna, Hell)
dom: The abode of punishment; the Fire, conceived as seven-layered with seven gates
note: The most common Qur'anic name for Hell (jahannam, cognate of Gehenna); abundantly attested (e.g. Q 4:140, 15:43-44). Also the name of one of the seven levels.

name: The Seven Gates of Hell (abwab jahannam)
dom: The set of seven gates/levels of Jahannam, each apportioned to a class of the damned
note: Qur'an 15:44 'it has seven gates, to each gate a portion assigned.' Classical sources name seven descending levels; modeled here as the structuring set.

name: Lazaa (the Blazing Flame)
dom: A level/name of Hell, the blazing fire that tears away the scalp
note: Qur'anic lazaa (Q 70:15-16). In classical seven-level schemes counted among the gates/levels of Jahannam.

name: al-Hutamah (the Crusher)
dom: A level/name of Hell, the consuming fire that crushes and that leaps over the hearts
note: Qur'anic al-hutama (Q 104:4-9). Counted among the seven levels/gates of Hell in classical eschatology (Lange).

name: Saʿir (the Blaze)
dom: A level/name of Hell, the blazing fire prepared for the disbelievers
note: Qur'anic al-saʿir, frequent (e.g. Q 4:10, 67:5). Counted among the seven levels/gates of Jahannam.

name: Saqar (the Scorching Fire)
dom: A level/name of Hell, the scorching fire that spares nothing, with nineteen keepers over it
note: Qur'anic saqar (Q 74:26-30, 54:48). One of the named levels/gates of Hell; associated with the nineteen guardians.

name: al-Jahim (the Hellfire)
dom: A level/name of Hell, the fierce blazing fire
note: Qur'anic al-jahim, frequent (e.g. Q 2:119, 5:10). Counted among the seven levels/gates of Jahannam in classical schemes.

name: al-Hawiyah (the Abyss)
dom: A level/name of Hell, the bottomless pit that is the 'mother/refuge' of the damned with light scales
note: Qur'anic al-hawiya (Q 101:9-11). Often taken as the deepest level of Hell in classical seven-fold schemes (Lange).

name: Barzakh (the intermediate state)
dom: The barrier/interspace between death and resurrection in which the dead await the Last Day; the realm of grave-life
note: Qur'anic barzakh (Q 23:100), developed in hadith and theology as the intermediate realm where Munkar and Nakir question the dead. Central to classical eschatology (Lange).

name: As-Sirat (the bridge over Hell)
dom: The bridge stretched over Jahannam that all must cross at the Judgment, finer than a hair and sharper than a sword
note: Eschatological al-sirat of hadith (drawing on Qur'anic sirat imagery, Q 37:23-24); the bridge to Paradise over Hell. Standard in classical accounts (Lange).

name: al-Aʿraf (the Heights)
dom: The elevated places/partition between Paradise and Hell, occupied by those whose scales are balanced
note: Qur'anic al-aʿraf (Q 7:46-48), names Sura 7; the heights with the Men of the Aʿraf who see both abodes. A liminal realm in the cosmic geography.

name: Sidrat al-Muntaha (the Lote-Tree of the Boundary)
dom: The lote-tree marking the utmost boundary of the seventh heaven, near the Garden of Refuge (Jannat al-Maʾwa)
note: Qur'anic sidrat al-muntaha (Q 53:14-15), reached at the Miʿraj, beside jannat al-maʾwa. The cosmic boundary-tree at the limit of created knowledge.
